# Mathematical Background {#sec-math}

This appendix collects the mathematical tools used in the book. It is not a
substitute for a quantum mechanics course; rather, it provides just enough
formalism to read the code and proofs.

## Linear Algebra Essentials

### Vectors and Inner Products

A quantum state of $n$ qubits is a unit vector in $\mathbb{C}^{2^n}$:

$$|\psi\rangle = \sum_{i=0}^{2^n-1} \alpha_i |i\rangle, \quad \sum_i |\alpha_i|^2 = 1$$

The *inner product* of two states $|\psi\rangle$ and $|\phi\rangle$:

$$\langle\psi|\phi\rangle = \sum_i \alpha_i^* \beta_i \in \mathbb{C}$$

The *fidelity* (overlap squared):

$$F(\psi, \phi) = |\langle\psi|\phi\rangle|^2 \in [0, 1]$$

### Tensor Products

For two-qubit systems, the basis states are tensor products:

$$|00\rangle = |0\rangle \otimes |0\rangle, \quad |01\rangle = |0\rangle \otimes |1\rangle, \quad \ldots$$

The state of a product (non-entangled) system:

$$|\psi_A\rangle \otimes |\psi_B\rangle$$

### Density Matrices

A *pure state* $|\psi\rangle$ can equivalently be described by its density matrix:

$$\rho = |\psi\rangle\langle\psi|$$

For a system with subsystems $A$ (latent) and $B$ (trash), the *partial trace*
gives the reduced state of $A$:

$$\rho_A = \text{Tr}_B[\rho]$$

## Quantum Gates as Matrices

Single-qubit gates act on $\mathbb{C}^2$; they are $2 \times 2$ unitary matrices.

### Rotation Gates

$$R_X(\theta) = e^{-i\theta X/2} = \begin{pmatrix}\cos(\theta/2) & -i\sin(\theta/2) \\ -i\sin(\theta/2) & \cos(\theta/2)\end{pmatrix}$$

$$R_Y(\theta) = e^{-i\theta Y/2} = \begin{pmatrix}\cos(\theta/2) & -\sin(\theta/2) \\ \sin(\theta/2) & \cos(\theta/2)\end{pmatrix}$$

$$R_Z(\theta) = e^{-i\theta Z/2} = \begin{pmatrix}e^{-i\theta/2} & 0 \\ 0 & e^{i\theta/2}\end{pmatrix}$$

Applied to $|0\rangle$:

$$R_Y(\theta)|0\rangle = \cos\!\tfrac{\theta}{2}|0\rangle + \sin\!\tfrac{\theta}{2}|1\rangle$$
$$\Rightarrow\quad P(|0\rangle) = \cos^2(\theta/2), \quad P(|1\rangle) = \sin^2(\theta/2)$$

## Measurements and Observables

### Expectation Value

For observable $\hat{O}$ and state $|\psi\rangle$:

$$\langle\hat{O}\rangle = \langle\psi|\hat{O}|\psi\rangle$$

For PauliZ on qubit 0:

$$\langle Z_0 \rangle = P(|0\rangle) - P(|1\rangle) \in [-1, +1]$$

### Pauli Operators

$$X = \begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}, \quad Y = \begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix}, \quad Z = \begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$$

## Variational Principle

A *variational circuit* parameterises a unitary:

$$U(\boldsymbol{\theta}) = \prod_{l} U_l(\theta_l)$$

where each $U_l(\theta_l) = e^{-i\theta_l H_l/2}$ for some Hermitian generator $H_l$.

The model output is:

$$f(\mathbf{x}; \boldsymbol{\theta}) = \langle 0|U^\dagger(\boldsymbol{\theta})\,\phi^\dagger(\mathbf{x})\, \hat{O}\, \phi(\mathbf{x})\,U(\boldsymbol{\theta})|0\rangle$$

## Parameter-Shift Rule

For generators with two eigenvalues $\pm r$:

$$\frac{\partial f}{\partial \theta_l} = r\left[f\!\left(\theta_l + \frac{\pi}{4r}\right) - f\!\left(\theta_l - \frac{\pi}{4r}\right)\right]$$

For standard Pauli rotations ($r = 1/2$, shift $= \pi/2$):

$$\frac{\partial f}{\partial \theta_l} = \frac{f(\theta_l + \pi/2) - f(\theta_l - \pi/2)}{2}$$

This is exact (not an approximation) and requires exactly 2 circuit evaluations per
parameter.

## Loss Functions

### Mean Squared Error (MSE)

$$\text{MSE} = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N (y_i - \hat{y}_i)^2$$

Used for regression (Chapters 4–5).

### R² (Coefficient of Determination)

$$R^2 = 1 - \frac{\sum_i(y_i - \hat{y}_i)^2}{\sum_i(y_i - \bar{y})^2}$$

$R^2 \in (-\infty, 1]$; $R^2 = 1$ is perfect fit.

### Binary Cross-Entropy (BCE)

$$\mathcal{L}_\text{BCE} = -\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N\left[y_i \log \hat{p}_i + (1-y_i)\log(1-\hat{p}_i)\right]$$

Used for classification (Chapters 6–8). Requires $\hat{p}_i \in (0, 1)$.

### Sigmoid

$$\sigma(z) = \frac{1}{1 + e^{-z}} \in (0, 1)$$

Maps logits (real values) to probabilities.

## SWAP Test

The SWAP test circuit estimates fidelity without direct state access:

$$P(\text{ancilla} = |0\rangle) = \frac{1 + |\langle\psi|\phi\rangle|^2}{2}$$

$$\Rightarrow\quad F(\psi,\phi) = |\langle\psi|\phi\rangle|^2 = 2P(|0\rangle_\text{anc}) - 1$$

## Mackey-Glass Equation

$$\frac{dx(t)}{dt} = \frac{\beta\,x(t-\tau)}{1 + x(t-\tau)^n} - \gamma\,x(t)$$

| Parameter | Typical value | Role |
|-----------|--------------|------|
| $\beta$ | 0.2 | Positive feedback strength |
| $\gamma$ | 0.1 | Decay rate |
| $\tau$ | 17 | Delay (controls chaos) |
| $n$ | 10 | Nonlinearity exponent |

For $\tau > 16.8$, the system exhibits chaotic dynamics. For $\tau \leq 16.8$, it
converges to a limit cycle.
